text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert fired: autoscale-throttle-high-prod. Pager routed to alex (oncall).

alex (oncall): I'm looking. seeing lots of short-lived throttle spikes and autoscale flapping. queue_depth alarms firing first then tokens/sec spike.

maya (oncall): copying in sam and katie. customer-facing API latency up ~300ms for a subset of requests? some retries visible.

alex (oncall): confirmed. pattern: burst of requests -> queue depth jumps -> scaler reacts -> pods churn -> KV cache miss -> more latency -> more requests pile up. looks like a feedback loop.

sam (ml-infra): hmm. metrics show throttle_events spiked from 0 to ~250 in 2m between 10:23–10:25 UTC. tokens/sec also doubled on model-serving pool. autoscaler targetUtilization is 0.65 with cool-down 30s.

alex (oncall): immediate mitigation: 1) increase alert debounce and lower page severity 2) temporarily raise queue_depth threshold for autoscale page 3) pin fallback model variant for heavy tails. doing 1 & 2 now.

katie (platform): 👍 please post the exact alert change so we can revert in postmortem.

alex (oncall): changing Prometheus rule (temporary):
```yaml
- alert: HighQueueDepth
  expr: sum(prod_queue_depth{service="model-serve"}) by (pool) > 180
  for: 3m  # was 1m
  labels:
    severity: warning  # was page
```
made the rule soft-warning and extended `for` to 3m. patched via /ops/prometheus-reload.

incident-bot: Patch applied by alex (oncall).

maya (oncall): I muted the PagerDuty escalation for HighQueueDepth for the next 30m while we observe. leaving page for throttle_events.

jordan (sre): created a quick Grafana panel: tokens/sec per node + throttle_events/5m. link: https://grafana.internal/d/xyz/model-serve-signal (pinned).

sam (ml-infra): digging into autoscaler logs: saw a flurry of ScaleUp -> ScaleDown within ~2-3min windows. cool-down too short for our model cold-start cost. recommended change: increase cooldown to 180s and change stabilization window.

alex (oncall): good call. I'll apply a temporary override to the k8s HPA-like config: set stabilizationWindowSeconds: 180 and targetUtilization -> 0.75 for prod-model-pool.

katie (platform): note: raising targetUtilization increases chance of throttles, but reduces churn/cold-starts. this is a tradeoff — we'll monitor tokens/sec and latency.

alex (oncall): applied override: `kubectl patch hpa model-pool-prod -p '{"spec": {"behavior": {"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 180}}}}'` and bumped target to 75% via config-manager.

maya (oncall): monitoring dashboards now. early signal: queue depth back to baseline in ~6m, throttle_events trending down, latency improving.

sam (ml-infra): started a short-run synthetic load test to validate behavior under burst. will share results in 20m.

jordan (sre): action item logged: update runbook to include:
- adjust queue_depth alert gates to be correlated with tokens/sec and throttle_events
- add 3m debounce for autoscale pages
- create a dashboard with per-pool token burn, queue depth, throttle_events and pod churn timeline
- recommend default HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds 180s for model-serving pools

alex (oncall): filing a post-incident ticket: INFRA-2342 (autoscale signal refactor). assigning to sam + katie + jordan. will include playbook edits, alert rule PR, and a dashboard template.

katie (platform): also add a short-term mitigation play: when throttle spike detected -> escalate to human only if throttle_events > 50 sustained for 5m AND tokens/sec > 2x baseline. that reduces noisy pages during surface-level bursts.

maya (oncall): customer impact: looked at request traces; ~0.4% of requests experienced degraded latency during the peak window (10:22–10:28 UTC). no errors surfaced, retries absorbed by clients. will add this to the incident summary.

alex (oncall): marking on-call handoff in 15m. leaving notes in the oncall doc. if anything regresses ping @maya directly.

incident-bot: Incident state changed to: mitigated.

sam (ml-infra): follow-up: I'm going to prototype a composite alert that requires both queue_depth AND throttle_events to fire the pager. will post a draft alert rule in #eng-sre-drafts.

jordan (sre): great. let's also record the cost impact: temporary HPA changes increased average pod-hours by ~8% during the window — include in the postmortem.

alex (oncall): thanks team. summary: temp alert debounce + threshold bump, HPA stabilization increase, dashboard + synthetic test, postmortem + runbook updates. I'll close the page after the handoff. :white_check_mark:

maya (oncall): taking night shift, I'll monitor for the next hour and kick off the postmortem doc. thanks all.

---
Post-incident follow-ups (to be done):
- sam: PR for composite alert + test harness (due +3d)
- katie: dashboard template + runbook PR (due +4d)
- jordan: cost impact analysis (due +5d)
- alex/maya: incident write-up and timeline (due +2d)
